column1: In the previous chapters, we have examined models that explain the economy both in the long run and in the short run. It might seem that, in some sense, our study of macroeconomic theory is complete. But to believe so would be a mistake. Like all scientists, economists never rest. There are always more questions to be answered, more refinements to be made. In this chapter and the next two, we look at some advances in macroeconomic theory that expand and refine our understanding of the forces that govern the economy.
